latest_release.name: Purge v1.14.1
latest_release.body:
## Release highlights

- **Uninstall Purge**: Settings and the Purge menu can now remove Purge itself. It turns off its background parts first, then moves itself to the Trash, with settings and history too if you choose.
- **Suites show as one entry**: In the App Uninstaller, apps from one vendor that share a folder, like DaVinci Resolve's four, show as one group you can open, tick as a whole, or pick from one by one.
- **Vendor uninstallers come first**: When a suite has its own uninstaller, Purge points you to it, and warns before you remove only part of the suite.

## What's changed

* feat: add Uninstall Purge (#330) by @jithin-sabu in #338
* feat: group a vendor's apps that share a folder in the App Uninstaller (#155) by @jithin-sabu in #337

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jithin-sabu/purge-app/compare/v1.14.0...v1.14.1

See the assets below to download and install this version.

detail.readme_excerpt:
Purge

Free up your Mac. Safely.

English | 简体中文

A free, open-source native Mac app that clears the cache and junk your Mac piles up on its own.
Files go to the Trash by default, so you can put them back.

Download  ·  Install guide  ·  Build from source  ·  Security

--- Your Mac quietly fills up with cache and junk you never see and never asked for. Purge finds it, marks what is safe, and clears it in one click. > [!NOTE] > Files and folders go to the Trash by default, and Purge never empties the Trash, so you can put them back until you empty it yourself. Removed for good: iOS simulators and simulator runtimes, through Xcode's `simctl`; Time Machine local snapshots, through `tmutil` (Purge keeps the newest and the one from your last backup); the Apple Intelligence models on macOS 27, which Apple's asset service releases and Purge can download again; command-line tools and Homebrew cask apps that their package manager uninstalls, when you choose that in the review sheet.
